probes.why: The three reads tests/wirefeed cannot construct offline. On the first tick with a non-null CR15NetGame it reports the RAW qword at +0x28C8 - the one runtime fact W1-L section 4 argued for and could not run - then registers the shipped IWiretap on SR15NetPlayerStateMsg, SR15NetReplicatedDeltaUnreliableVars and SR15NetComponentEvent, records the thread each callback arrives on against the tick thread, observes 60 s, calls UnlistenAll and watches 10 s of silence. It also re-reads the five entry-point prologues and hashes .text before the first Listen and after the last, which is the W1-L half of SC7. The offline feed check already proved the mechanism against a recorded session at 44.02 Hz; what this adds is the three inputs that had no constructible form without a live client.
probes.scope: THREE LIMITS, stated before the run. (1) ZERO CALLBACKS IS NOT A FAILURE HERE and the probe reports it as COULD-NOT-DETERMINE: an offline local match may legitimately carry no traffic on these symbols, and this probe cannot tell a quiet session from a wrong bus. tests/wirefeed is what separates those, offline, against a capture where the traffic is known to exist - so do not quote a non-zero count here as the rate check, and do not quote a zero as a defect. (2) This is NOT the SC7 runtime half. A diff declaring zero expected rows is refused by design (HARNESS section 7) and a Level-0 packet has zero rows to declare; what is established is the negative contribution, that W1-L adds nothing to whatever the ledger predicts. (3) The broadcaster read is one sample from one session on one profile; it settles whether a client-mode netgame carries a broadcaster, not whether it always does.
probes.timeoutJustification: 60 s of observation plus 10 s of post-teardown silence, both of which only start once a CR15NetGame exists, plus the session load ahead of them. The probe's own worker files a real verdict at 200 s whatever phase it reached, so it never holds the launch to the deadline: 240 s is headroom over that, not a wait on a game state that may not arrive.
